summary:
1. High-performing hooks directly target the viewer's body or daily sensory experiences using second-person pronouns in the first 3 words.
2. Winning titles use simple, curiosity-gap phrasing ('Why [Universal Everyday Phenomenon] [Action]') without relying on clickbait emojis.
3. Universal human/everyday biology topics significantly beat niche engineering or outdoor scenario topics in swipe resistance (stayed_pct >47% vs <30%).
4. Low-stayed hooks waste the critical first second on hypothetical story setups ('Your car swerves...') or passive preamble ('Fossilized bones can...').
5. Shorter, punchy scripts that deliver immediate present-tense facts sustain higher swipe-away retention than narrative setups exceeding 30 seconds.
winning_hooks: Start immediately with present-tense direct address about the viewer's body ('Your eyes are... right now').
State a rapid, counter-intuitive assertion about an everyday action ('You are not sad when...').
Keep opening hook sentences under 10 words to deliver the core curiosity trigger instantly.
avoid: Avoid hypothetical roleplay scenarios ('Your car swerves off...') that take too long to establish context.
Avoid niche topics that apply only to specific viewers ('Your frozen pond...').
Avoid passive background statements that delay the main surprise ('Fossilized bones can last millions of years...').
next_experiment: A/B test a standard body-focused direct hook ('Your skin is shedding thousands of cells right now') against a hypothetical scenario hook ('If you collected all the skin you shed in a year...') on the exact same topic and duration (<25s) to measure stayed_pct impact.
